title: Kernel and support description of a sheaf strict transform
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $Z\subseteq S$ be a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose defining ideal is finite-type quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], let $b:S'=\operatorname{Bl}_Z(S)\to S$ [def-nagata-global-blowup], and let $f:X\to S$ be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme]. For a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent], write $p:X\times_S S'\to X$ for the projection and $\mathcal F^{\mathrm{st}}$ for its module strict transform [def-trf-module-strict-transform]. The canonical map $p^*\mathcal F\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal F^{\mathrm{st}}$ is surjective; its kernel is the subsheaf of local sections supported on $(f\circ p)^{-1}(Z)$, and this kernel is a quasi-coherent submodule, so $\mathcal F^{\mathrm{st}}$ is a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_{X\times_SS'}$-module. Consequently the map is an isomorphism over the complement of that inverse image, and $\mathcal F^{\mathrm{st}}$ has no nonzero local sections supported on $(f\circ p)^{-1}(Z)$. When $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, the kernel of $\mathcal O_{X\times_SS'}\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O_X^{\mathrm{st}}$ is the ideal sheaf of the scheme strict transform $i:X'\hookrightarrow X\times_SS'$ of $X$ along $b$ relative to $U=S\setminus Z$ [def-nagata-strict-transform], so that $\mathcal O_X^{\mathrm{st}}\cong i_*\mathcal O_{X'}$ as quotients of $\mathcal O_{X\times_SS'}$.

proof.text: Put $Y=X\times_SS'$ with projections $p,q$, $E=b^{-1}Z$, $D=q^{-1}E$ and $V=Y\setminus D$. The identity $b\circ q=f\circ p$ from [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $D=(f\circ p)^{-1}Z$. By [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center], $E$ is locally principal. The pullback $H=p^*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent]. Apply [lem-trf-locally-principal-supported-kernel] to $q,E,H$: the open inclusion $j:V\hookrightarrow Y$ is qcqs, and its restriction kernel $K\subseteq H$ is quasi-coherent and consists exactly of sections supported on $D$.

source.place: Tag 07ZT, lemma-complement-locally-principal-closed-subscheme; lemma-pullback-locally-principal; paragraph preceding Tag 080D, definition-strict-transform. Quasi-coherence and sectionwise kernel: properties.tex Tag 07ZP, lemma-sections-supported-on-closed-subset, especially proof of (3).

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-supported-quotient-saturation] to $Y,V,H,K$. It gives a quasi-coherent quotient $Q$, an epimorphism $H\to Q$ with sectionwise kernel $K$, an isomorphism after restriction to $V$, and no nonzero local sections of $Q$ supported on $D$. By [def-trf-module-strict-transform], $Q=\mathcal F^{\mathrm{st}}$ with its canonical quotient map. By the sheaf axiom a local section of $Q$ (or of $H$) is supported on $D$ exactly when it restricts to zero on its intersection with $V$, so the last conclusion says that $\mathcal F^{\mathrm{st}}$ has no nonzero local section supported on $D$. Since $D=(f\circ p)^{-1}Z$ by Step 1, these are all the module assertions.

source.place: Tag 07ZP, lemma-sections-supported-on-closed-subset, exact restriction-kernel sequence in the proof of (3); quotient consequence used in divisors.tex Tag 080D (1), definition-strict-transform. Residual-support vanishing is the affine-lifting argument of the returned item step 3, not a separately stated clause of Tag 07ZP.

proof.text: For $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, put $U=S\setminus Z$ and let $j:\Omega=Y\times_SU\hookrightarrow Y$ be the preimage of $U$ under $f\circ p=b\circ q$. Since $b^{-1}U=S'\setminus E$, $\Omega=q^{-1}(S'\setminus E)=V$, and by the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] the preserved open $(X\times_SU)\times_U(S'\times_SU)$ is canonically $V$, mapping to $Y$ by $j$, which is qcqs by Step 1. On an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $S$ where the ideal of $Z$ is $I=(a_1,\ldots,a_n)$, the $A$-algebra $A/I$ is presented with no generators and the relations $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, so $Z\hookrightarrow S$ is a finite-presentation centre and by [def-nagata-strict-transform] and [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-closure] $i:X'\hookrightarrow Y$ is the scheme-theoretic image $\operatorname{SIm}(j)$. Apply [lem-trf-finite-center-open-closure-kernel-data] to $f\circ p:Y\to S$ and the ideal of $Z$: $J=\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to j_*\mathcal O_V)$ is quasi-coherent and $i_*\mathcal O_{X'}=\mathcal O_Y/J$ as quotients of $\mathcal O_Y$, so $J$ is the ideal sheaf of $i$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]; sectionwise $J(W)=\ker(\mathcal O_Y(W)\to\mathcal O_Y(W\cap V))$. The canonical map $\epsilon:p^*\mathcal O_X\to\mathcal O_Y$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-structure-sheaf]; it commutes with restriction, so it carries the restriction kernel $K$ of Step 1 onto $J$. Hence $\epsilon$ induces $\mathcal O_X^{\mathrm{st}}=p^*\mathcal O_X/K\cong\mathcal O_Y/J=i_*\mathcal O_{X'}$, compatible with the quotient maps from $p^*\mathcal O_X\cong\mathcal O_Y$, and the kernel of $\mathcal O_Y\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O_X^{\mathrm{st}}$ is the ideal sheaf of $X'$.

lean.statement: theorem moduleStrictTransform_properties {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (I : S.IdealSheafData) [I.toModules.IsFiniteType] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] : Epi (moduleStrictTransformπ f I F) ∧ (∀ (V : (Limits.pullback f I.blowupMap).Opens) (s : Γ((tensorPullback (pullback.fst f I.blowupMap)).obj F, V)), (moduleStrictTransformπ f I F).app V s = 0 ↔ (moduleStrictTransformRestriction f I F).app V s = 0) ∧ (moduleStrictTransformKernel f I F).IsQuasicoherent ∧ (moduleStrictTransform f I F).IsQuasicoherent ∧ IsIso ((restrictFunctor (moduleStrictTransformOpen f I).ι).map (moduleStrictTransformπ f I F)) ∧ (∀ (V : (Limits.pullback f I.blowupMap).Opens) (s : Γ(moduleStrictTransform f I F, V)), ((restrictAdjunction (moduleStrictTransformOpen f I).ι).unit.app (moduleStrictTransform f I F)).app V s = 0 → s = 0)
